## Natural history notes

A large wolf spider characterized by its robust body, long legs, and brown to grayish-brown coloration with darker striping on the cephalothorax and abdomen. In Florida, it is found in leaf litter, lawns, fields, pine flatwoods, forest edges, gardens, and other ground-level habitats with open space for hunting and nearby cover. It does not build a prey-capturing web; instead, it actively hunts insects and other arthropods on the ground, often moving at night and sheltering under debris, vegetation, or other cover during the day.
